correctness.rationale: The exact 255-form search is complete because seven independent evaluation constraints leave an 8-dimensional binary quartic space. The 24 F2-pointwise nonsingular survivors have unit Jacobian ideals on all three affine charts, proving geometric smoothness. Every pair is tested for closure under addition: precisely eight disjoint triples. Explicit enumeration of GL3(F2) verifies one orbit with stabilizer 21. An independent matrix computation classifies all 48 irreducible 3x3 binary matrices into eight Singer subgroups and rules out mixed-group smooth pencils. For a representative pair, Groebner leading monomials X^2, XY^2, Y^11 establish affine length 13; explicit ideal inclusion and matching lengths prove the decomposition into four affine rational points and a local degree-nine residual component supported at one degree-three point. Three transverse rational infinity points complete the Bezout length 16. Exact scripts at relative paths verify_pencils.py and verify_matrix_pencils.py were executed successfully. No infinite-field extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The 2009 matrix and automorphism results classify individual smooth plane-filling quartics but neither the complete additive smooth-pencil incidence nor the scheme-theoretic triple residual base point. The 2022 paper poses the rationally smooth pencil problem and gives general and quadric/conic results, not this constrained extremal binary quartic classification. The 2023 work addresses higher-degree filling curves. Searches of published mathematical records and recovered earlier claims did not identify an equivalent or dominating result; priority risk from older unpublished computations is explicit. The 2022 unrestricted smooth-net existence theorem does not cover the sharply smaller plane-filling subspace where no smooth net exists.

value.rationale: The 2022 smooth-pencil question and minimum-degree plane-filling problem meet in the canonical small field F2. The full eight-pencil partition and sharp maximal linear-subspace dimension solve a finite but natural extremal classification. The Singer-group structure and nonreduced triple base points are geometric information needed to understand the resulting pencil maps and their resolutions, not an arbitrary invariant or a routine renaming. The result does not pretend to settle larger-field cases.
